# Martha Henstridge (~1854–1921)

**Role:** Second wife of John Telfer (1840–1913)

After the death of his first wife Martha Allen (1840–1876), John Telfer (1840–1913) married Martha Clara Henstridge on 28 Dec 1876 at the Residence of J. Telfer, Tantanoola Creek, South Australia.

**Born:** 22 Jan 1854, South Australia
**Died:** 13 Nov 1921, Adelaide, South Australia (aged 67)
**Buried:** Tantanoola Cemetery, Tantanoola SA

Martha was the daughter of Frederick Henstridge Sr. and Maria Smith. She had 10 children with John Telfer: Mark, Maria Clara, Isabella Lucieton, John Roland, Clara Blanche, Robert Freddy, Douglas, Colin Roy, Alan Dale, and Alma Tressy.

**Sources:**
1. **WikiTree:** [Martha Clara Henstridge (Henstridge-4)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Henstridge-4) — birth 22 Jan 1854, marriage 28 Dec 1876, death 13 Nov 1921 (GenealogySA records)
2. **FindAGrave:** [Martha Clara Telfer (memorial 186972464)](https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/186972464/martha-clara-telfer) — burial at Tantanoola Cemetery
3. **GenealogySA:** Death record Ade sym H B 450 P 228 — Martha died 13 Nov 1921, aged 68, widow, of Tantanoola
4. **Book:** *From the Borders to the Bush*

## Family Stories

After the death of his first wife, John Telfer married for the second time on 28th December 1876. His second wife was Martha Clara Henstridge, daughter of Frederick Henstridge. The marriage took place at John's private residence at Tantanoola Creek, officiated by the Rev. Charles Tresize. John was described as a "Stockholder", aged 34, and Martha as a Spinster, aged 23.

Martha came from a family with a remarkable history. An old letter preserved in the family tells the story: "When John Telfer took Martha Henstridge to wife, he married into a family with a great historic heritage." The Henstridge family is descended from the Viking Hengest, who came to England as a mercenary to assist King Vertigen of Kent, but overthrew him and ruled Kent for a number of years. His descendants fought the Normans in Sherwood Forest with Robin Hood. The heir to Hengest-Ridge Castle was given a baroncy by King John, and the barons kept the manuscripts to Magna Carta secretly in Hengestridge Castle until the King was forced to sign them.

Martha was very supportive of her husband in all his activities. She was an active member of the Tantanoola Red Cross, and served as Postmistress at Tantanoola from 1919 to 1921 after her daughter Tressic. Martha died in 1921 and is buried alongside John at Tantanoola Cemetery, where her headstone reads: "Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord."

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp. 238–240)*

## Life Summary

Martha Telfer was born on 18 April 1873 at Black Heath (also recorded as Blackheath), Tungkillo, South Australia, the fourth child and third daughter of John Telfer (1840–1913) by his first wife [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]]. The family lived at Honeysuckle Flat and Black Heath during her early years before moving to the Tantanoola district in the South East.

On 29 March 1899 at Tantanoola, SA, Martha married Malcolm Duncan Cameron (1873–1935), a farmer. They had at least one known child: a son, Malcolm Murray Cameron, born 2 August 1905 at Mount Gambier SA.

Martha died on 4 August 1964 at Mount Gambier, South Australia, aged 91, and was predeceased by her husband by 29 years. Her burial location has not been positively identified — no FindAGrave record has been found, and her 1964 death was too late for Trove newspaper death notices.

## Family Stories

Martha — known as Mattie — was the fourth and youngest child of John Telfer and his first wife Martha Allen, born on 18 April 1873 at Black Heath. She married Malcolm Duncan Cameron on 29 March 1899 at Tantanoola. Malcolm was a man of public affairs: during his time in Parliament he served on the Works Committee, eventually becoming its Chairman, and was a lifelong member of the Liberal Party. He was also an Elder of the Presbyterian Church for thirty years.

Mattie and Malcolm raised five children — Murray, Ivan, Lorna, Mavis and Jack — in the South East district. Malcolm died on 1 March 1935, and Mattie lived on for another twenty-nine years, passing away at Mount Gambier in 1964 at the age of 91.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp.238–239)*

body_markdown:
# Richard Paynter (1838–1869)

**Role:** First husband of Jean Telfer
**Born:** ~1838 — Cornwall, England
**Died:** 7 February 1869 (aged 30) — St. Kitts Creek, pleurisy
**Buried:** Kapunda area

Richard Paynter was born in Cornwall, England, the son of Richard Paynter of Calstock. He emigrated to South Australia where he worked as a labourer at Chain of Ponds.

He married Jean Telfer on 12 September 1859 at the Chain of Ponds Parsonage, solemnised by John Kither and witnessed by her father Francis Telfer and Henry Whiting. Jean was several months pregnant at the time.

After their first child Thomas was born, the family moved to Koppio near Port Lincoln where Richard worked as a shepherd for Jean's cousin James Telfer. They later returned to the Chain of Ponds area and then to St. Kitts between Kapunda and Truro, where Richard became the local school teacher — a change brought on by his failing health.

Richard died of pleurisy at the age of 30, leaving a widow and five children unprovided for.

**Source:** *From the Borders to the Bush* — Chapter on Jean/Jane Telfer

## Family Stories

Richard Paynter was born in Calstock, Cornwall, the son of Richard Paynter, who died in January 1856 aged 39 after "a protracted affliction." Richard the younger emigrated to South Australia and worked as a labourer at Chain of Ponds. On 12 September 1859, at just 19 years old, Jean Telfer married 21-year-old Richard Paynter at the Chain of Ponds Parsonage — a different setting from her sisters, who were married in their father Francis's home. Jean was several months pregnant at the time. After their first son Thomas was born, the family moved to Koppio near Port Lincoln, where Richard worked as a shepherd for Jean's cousin James Telfer. They later returned to the Chain of Ponds area and eventually settled at St. Kitts, between Kapunda and Truro. There, as Richard's health began to fail, he made an unusual career change — from shepherd to school teacher. The book records that he died of pleurisy on 7 February 1869 at St. Kitts Creek, aged just 30, leaving his widow and five children unprovided for. An in memoriam notice was placed in a local newspaper. His first child Dinah was born at Finniss Point five months after his death.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, p.16)*

## Life Summary
Robert Dunlop Lawrie was born at Craigman, New Cumnock, Ayrshire, Scotland on 23 May 1850, the son of John Lawrie (1810–1888) and Janet Dunlop (?–1902). His father farmed at Craigman before emigrating to South Australia in 1853 aboard the *Ann Dashwood*, arriving in Melbourne on 10 November 1853. Robert was approximately 3 years old at the time of emigration.

The family settled at Myponga Hills above Willunga, SA. Robert later farmed at "Bleak Farm," Long Plains, South Australia.

He married Caroline Hosking on 3 July 1879 at the Church of Christ, Alma, South Australia. They had nine children together.

He died on 26 November 1917 at Long Plains, South Australia.

# Ruth Telfer

**Role:** Youngest daughter of Francis Charles Telfer and Amy Ellen Telfer (née Provis) — sister of Murray John Telfer
**Born:** 26 October 1931 — Saddleworth, South Australia
**Parents:** [[Francis Charles Telfer (1875–1954)]] & [[Amy Ellen Telfer (1884–1951)]]
**Brother:** [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]]
**Siblings:** Francis Kelson, Clarice May, Emily Amelia, Jean, Gladys, Doris, Edwin Roy, Reginald Masters, Murray

---

## Life Summary

Ruth Telfer was the **youngest** of the ten Telfer children born to Francis and Amy Telfer. She was born at **Saddleworth**, South Australia, on 26 October 1931 — her birth name was **Pamela Ruth Telfer**, but the family called her Ruth.

Her sister Jean McMurtrie wrote in her memoir:

> \"Our youngest sister Ruth was born while we were at Saddleworth, mother was 48, and that was very hard for her, but Ruth being so much younger than the rest of us has been a real blessing to us all.\"

Ruth appears in a cherished family photograph circa 1936 at approximately age 6, riding the family horse **Duchess** with her brother Murray (then aged ~12), accompanied by the family dog.

The photograph captures a tender moment of rural childhood on the Eyre Peninsula — Ruth beaming with joy in her bob haircut and light summer top, bare legs dangling, while Murray holds the reins responsibly. Duchess, a bay with distinctive white blaze and four white socks, was clearly a beloved family horse.

Further details of Ruth's life — marriage, children, later residence — are currently being researched.

---

## Photos

![Murray John Telfer and sister Ruth Telfer (aged 6) on Duchess the horse with family dog, circa 1936](../_assets/Murray and Ruth Telfer on Duchess the horse 1936.jpg)

*Murray John Telfer (aged ~12) and his sister Ruth Telfer (aged 6) on Duchess the horse with the family dog, circa 1936. Ruth's joyful smile and Murray's protective posture capture a classic sibling moment on the family farm.*

---

- Murray John Telfer profile: confirms Francis Charles Telfer and Amy Ellen Telfer as parents

## Life Summary

William Henry Parker was born on 13 April 1893 at Long Plains, South Australia, the seventh child and third son of Scottish-born William Humphrey Parker (1850–1926) and Hannah Baker (1855–1948). His father had migrated from Mossblown, Ayrshire, Scotland, to South Australia. His older sister Sophia Parker (1886–1918) married into the Lawrie family (Frank Lindsay Lawrie), creating a double connection between the Parker and Lawrie families.

William married Caroline Edna Lawrie on 29 March 1917 at the residence of R. D. Lawrie, Long Plains, solemnised by Pastor Ross Goodwin. They had five children: Avis (b. 1918), Howard (b. 1920), Sydney Hugh (b. 1922), William Humphrey (b. 1926), and Shirley Edna (b. 1929).

He was a farmer at Long Plains for most of his life. He died on 16 December 1968 near Owen, South Australia, aged 75, and was buried at Shannon Cemetery (Calomba Methodist Cemetery), SA, alongside his wife Caroline Edna (who predeceased him in 1957).

## Life Summary

William Humphrey Parker was born on 17 July 1850 at Ragged Hill, Mossblown, Ayrshire, Scotland, the son of David Parker (1822–1888) and Isabella Kelly (c. 1825–1867). He emigrated to South Australia with his family.

He married Hannah Baker on 21 August 1878 at the residence of the bride's parents, Virginia, South Australia. They had ten children — six daughters and four sons — born between 1879 and 1899.

He was a farmer who settled in the Long Plains area. Two of his children married into the Lawrie family: daughter Sophia married Frank Lindsay Lawrie, and son William Henry married Caroline Edna Lawrie (Frank's sister).

He died on 18 February 1926 at Lower Mitcham, South Australia, and was buried at Mitcham General Cemetery.

## Life Summary

David Parker was born on 29 June 1822 at Ragged Hill Farm, Tarbolton, Ayrshire, Scotland. He was christened on 13 July 1822 at Tarbolton, with parents listed as Hugh Parker and Christian Fulton.

He married Isabella Kelly on 9 August 1846 in Barony, Lanarkshire, Scotland. In the 1851 Scotland Census, he was recorded as a Victualler living at Wallace Street, Wallacetown, St Quivox, Ayrshire, with wife Isabella and infant son William H (age 1).

The family emigrated to South Australia in 1852 aboard the ship **Martin Luther** (arriving 4 May 1852 in Adelaide), travelling with wife Isabella and three children.

After Isabella's death on 6 July 1867, he married Clementina Minto on 20 June 1871 at Hailes House, Hackney, Adelaide.

He died on 4 April 1888 at his residence "Wheatlands", Hundred of Pirie, South Australia, aged 65, and was buried at Port Pirie Cemetery.

## Life Summary

Sophia Parker was born on 4 February 1886 at Long Plains, South Australia, the fourth child and third daughter of William Humphrey Parker and Hannah Baker.

She married Frank Lindsay Lawrie on 26 March 1915 at the Christian Chapel, Grote Street, Adelaide. Frank was the brother of Caroline Edna Lawrie, who married Sophia's brother William Henry Parker — creating a double Parker-Lawrie marriage connection.

Sophia died young on 29 March 1918 at Balaklava, South Australia, aged 32, just three years after her marriage. She was buried at Shannon Cemetery (Calomba Methodist Cemetery), SA.

**Note:** The Leads.md file referenced "Sue Lawrie Adoption" — this may relate to a Lawrie family connection through Frank Lindsay Lawrie's line, as his brother Robert Dunlop Lawrie's descendants include Lawrie family members.
